newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK bank giants muscle into blue-chip index.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK bank giants muscle into blue-chip index.

text.p: Two more banking giants will muscle their way into the FTSE 100 on Monday, elbowing aside two non-financial shares and beefing up the bank sector's already hefty presence in Britain's blue-chip share index.

Halifax Plc and Alliance & Leicester Plc, former building societies which converted to banks and floated on London's stock exchange over the last two months, join the index next week in its quarterly shake-up.
Despite a sharp fall in UK shares overall, Halifax and Alliance shares surged on Friday as institutions loaded up with stock ahead of their FTSE debut.
There is more than just pride at stake in entering the index -- institutions running funds which track the FTSE must buy up shares in new entrants to the index, and sell those that are shoved out.

Halifax saw particularly strong demand, climbing 26p to 771 with volume reaching 47 million shares shortly after the official close of London trading. It was the market's most active stock by a wide margin.
"We're seeing a lot of institutional demand," one market-maker said. "Weightings are still low."
Alliance & Leicester was also active, with volume of 11.7 million, though an earlier 24p gain failed to hold in the face of the market's sharp fall and the stock closed down 1/2p at 598-1/2.
Dealers said Halifax was marketing its shares aggressively and planning a series of meetings with brokers, which was fuelling interest in the stock.

Halifax, with a market capitalisation of around 19 billion pounds ($31 billion), will be the eighth largest company in the FTSE, while Alliance & Leicester will come in at number 67 with a capitalisation of about 12.5 billion.

Their inclusion will increase the retail banking sector's representation in the FTSE 100's capitalisation from around 18.5 percent to more than 21 percent. Financial stocks as a whole currently have a weighting of 24.09 percent.
However the increasing predominance of financials at the expense of other sectors is in line with trends in other markets.

The financials' weighting in the UK is smaller than the weighting of financial stocks in Germany's DAX index, which stands at 28.58 percent, but greater than their 18.34 percent weighting in France's CAC 40.

The presence of the financial sector in the FTSE is set to increase even further -- insurer Norwich Union Plc, which floated this week, is expected to join the index at its next reshuffle, while Woolwich, another building society converting to a bank, may also squeeze in before the end of the year.

The increasing weight of banking stocks in the FTSE could have important implications for its performance -- the sector has played a crucial role in driving the FTSE's record breaking rally over the past year.
The banking sector has outperformed the FTSE by around 35 percent in the last 12 months, a key factor in hauling the blue-chip index 24 percent higher over the period.
Without banks and pharmaceuticals, another strong sector over the past year, the FTSE's gains would have been paltry at best, analysts say.
Halifax and Alliance & Leicester will replace clothing retailer Burton Group Plc and healthcare and household products group Smith & Nephew Plc in the index.
